tb21_profile.skill: Infer the algorithm that produced a rendered artifact and re-derive it from scratch in C - ray/path-tracing maths, PPM output, numeric agreement to 0.99 L2 - under a hard source-size budget that forbids embedding the data
tb21_profile.domain: Computer graphics / offline rendering, PPM image format, C with libm, image similarity metrics
tb21_profile.task_form: reverse-engineer-an-artifact then implement-from-inference, with an optimise-for-a-budget constraint (source under 2KB gzipped) and a compile-and-run harness

verifier_notes: software-engineering_20260606_153537_023 is graded `weak` (0.182) but I read tests/test_outputs.py: it compiles nothing, it RUNS the ray tracer, pins the image to 200x200, checks the PPM P6 header, and asserts on the colour of specific pixels (green sphere at centre, red left, blue right, dark sky, plane brightness, >5 distinct colours). That is a real rendering check, not a file-exists check; the grade is a heuristic undercount and I treated it as usable. Separately, software-engineering_20260604_002443_015 and software-engineering_20260604_193356_016 are CalibForge 'binary environment analyzer' boilerplate whose last line says 'This task evaluates ... for the path-tracing domain' / 'path-tracing-reverse domain' - pure lexical bait with zero graphics content. They are excluded and the merge step should blacklist that template.

notes: CalibForge is the decisive new corpus for this task and it is not close. It contains what is plainly a sibling of the TB2.1 seed (software-engineering_20260503_030115_015: reconstruct a programmatically generated artifact to 0.99 normalized L2, don't read the reference, C source under 2KB gzipped, gcc -static -lm), an actual ray tracer implementation task, and an entire family of 'write C that emits a pixel-perfect image under a gzip source budget'. Nothing in the v1 pool comes near that. Warning for the merge step: CalibForge also contains a boilerplate 'binary environment analyzer' template (software-engineering_20260604_002443_015, software-engineering_20260604_193356_016 and likely siblings) whose closing line names the TB2.1 domain verbatim ('for the `path-tracing` domain'). Retrieval ranks those highly and they are worthless - the body is a generic directory-hashing script. Terminal-Lego contributes the image-similarity-metric angle (task_09110, task_14017) but has no rendering. TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis have essentially nothing graphical; their lists are honest 2s with declared filler at the bottom. SWE-Rebench is the weakest - only cadquery gives real 3D geometry - and ranks 6-10 are filler.
